subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find the equation of the circle passing through the point (2,3) and concentric with x² + y² + 8x + 12y + 15 = 0.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, SENIOR INTER MATHS-2B (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.78 — VSAQ chapter 12 Circle, answer 109.2. It is the right-hand twin of answer 109.1. No appearance tag is printed beside it. Every number was re-derived and the book is correct: k = −65 and the circle is x² + y² + 8x + 12y − 65 = 0. The mark split 1 + 1 is OURS, not the book’s: the whole VSAQ chapter is set in two columns and prints no margin tags anywhere. There is no printed 2-mark split in this book to pattern it on, so it splits the answer at its one natural break. Star rank: the book’s VSAQ chapter table (book p.76) and its VSAQ hit list header (book p.11) both give the CIRCLE VSAQ chapter ★★★, but the chapter header printed on book p.77 shows only ★★. The two disagree; the TABLE’s rank is used, so every Circle VSAQ entry takes stars 3. That rank belongs to the CHAPTER, not to this question. Paper position: Maths-2B Section A runs Q1-Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory; Circle holds Q1 and Q2. Neither a two-book union check nor a board back-test was possible for Maths-2B: there is no TSBIE second-year Basic Learning Material on hand, and answer-book/papers/ holds first-year physics only. The book’s five Guess Papers (book pp.118-127) are the only stand-in, and the orchestrator diffs the authored set against them. Everything on this card stays a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

insider_note: The given circle has a positive constant and the answer has a negative one, and that is expected: the new circle passes through a point far from the centre, so it is the larger of the two.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the concentric family
steps.margin_note: One mark. Copy +8x and +12y exactly and replace only the constant.
steps.memory_tip: Concentric circles share g and f. Only c changes.
lines: Concentric circles have the same centre,
so g and f are unchanged and only c differs.
steps.why: Since the centre is (−g, −f), keeping g and f keeps the centre. The constant alone sets the size of the circle.
common_mistakes: Keeping the original constant 15 as well as introducing k.
Halving 8 and 12 before writing the family.

steps.label: Substitute the point and solve
steps.memory_tip: Add the four numbers, then k is the negative of that total.
steps.why: Every term is positive here, so the sum is 65 and the constant must be −65 to make the equation vanish at the given point.
common_mistakes: Reporting k = 65 without the sign change.
